'Do you think Shruti and her parents would understand one another? If yes why, if no why not' -- a defended judgement, C-3.2. DEFECT: the stem carries the whole previous question plus its model answer before the real prompt.

The extract in which Shruti explains why she cannot tell her father, and the sub-questions identify her state as 'in a dilemma' and unpack 'the right way'. This is the tension of the play being set up, C-2.2-LO-25. Not C-2.1-LO-12: that outcome needs the play compared with the accompanying poem, and no poem appears here.

How cultural diversity contributes to the STORYLINE -- the Indo-Western band is both the plot's engine and its resolution (LO-25, tension built and released), and the substance is the meeting of Indian and Western musical traditions (C-4.2, richness of culture and heritage and their connections). Both cited because the question joins the two.

'What is an aside used for?' -- keyed to all three: showing thought and feeling, and linking character to audience directly. C-2.2-LO-26 exactly, and the concept tag 'Use of Aside' agrees. Not C-2.1-LO-11, which only asks the reader to NAME the features of dramatic form; this asks what the device does.
Choose non-lexical fillers -- whew, err, arrgh, hmmm, ahem-ahem -- to match emoticons. C-2.2-LO-28 names non-lexical fillers first among the things this chapter's language work covers.

The assessed element is the musical terminology, C-2.2-LO-28. DEFECT: the stem fuses a dictionary entry, page furniture ('NODIA') and an unrelated reading passage.

Report the Asma-and-Deepa dialogue in indirect speech, with the tense, pronoun and time shifts ('today' to 'that day', 'spilled' to 'had spilled'). C-2.2-LO-29 word for word. The concept tag 'Reported Speech' agrees.

Write a play script from a story opening, and the model answer supplies a title, a setting, a character list and bracketed stage directions. C-1.3-LO-7 exactly. Not C-1.2: the LO names the play-script form.

Why play dialogue takes no inverted commas -- a question about the LAYOUT convention of dramatic form, which is one of the features C-2.1-LO-11 asks the reader to name. Not LO-25: nothing about tension or structure.
What is written within brackets and what it conveys -- stage directions, named explicitly in C-2.1-LO-11.
How stage directions help the actors -- still the function of a named feature of dramatic form, C-2.1-LO-11. DEFECT: the answer ends with 'Click Here to Buy book on...'.

Mapped on the answers, which are the only usable part: the extract sets 'traditional values and modern expressions' against each other, plays on 'lost' as both losing one's roots and being physically apart, gives 'duty', and infers that Shruti will end up pursuing both without guilt. That is the play's tension and its release, C-2.2-LO-25. DEFECT: the stem is entirely the previous question plus its model answer plus an advert; the real extract and sub-questions are missing.

Justify the title 'Twin Melodies' and show how tradition and modernity are explored -- the two melodies are the two positions whose conflict the play builds and then resolves, C-2.2-LO-25. Not C-2.1-LO-12, which requires the accompanying poem to be brought in.

The three friends' differing attitudes to confronting authority, and what those reveal about each of them. Character reading from dialogue; no LO covers it (LO-28 is fillers, phrasal verbs and musical terms, not characterisation), so C-2.2 competency.

Analyse Nabin and how his attitude EVOLVES THROUGHOUT THE PLAY -- a change traced across the scenes, which is what C-2.2-LO-25 covers. A static character sketch would sit at C-2.2; this one is explicitly about movement.

How Shruti's internal conflict explores duty against passion -- the central tension of the play. C-2.2-LO-25. LO-26 was considered because the conflict surfaces in her aside, but the question asks about the conflict itself, not about what the aside device does.

Evaluate the conclusion and say whether it realistically resolves the conflicts. LO-25 for the release of tension across the scenes, C-3.2 because the item demands a verdict with reasons rather than a description.
The protagonist's name (Shruti) -- plain recall; this chapter has no LO for it, so C-2.2 competency.

She does not want to hurt him because she deeply RESPECTS him -- a stated attitude, recall, C-2.2 competency.
